recentUpdates: The possession date for units in Ansal API The Fernhill was slated for August 2018.

Homebuyers of Ansal Fernhill in Sector 91 protested against the developer due to the delayed possession of flats, even 11 years after the project's launch. Around 70 homebuyers claimed they had paid 95%-100% of the project cost but were yet to receive possession.

The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) initiated the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) against Ansal Properties & Infrastructure Ltd. The action was due to delays in the Fernhill project and alleged financial irregularities.

The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) agreed to initiate insolvency proceedings against Ansal Properties & Infrastructures (Ansal API) based on a petition filed by 126 buyers of 'The Fernhill' project in Sector 91, Gurugram, who alleged delays and defaults in project delivery. The promised possession period of 48 months, ending in July 2017, was not met, and the units remained incomplete even after a grace period that ended on January 30, 2018.
The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) confined the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process specifically to the Fernhill project, ensuring focused resolution efforts.

The Insolvency Resolution Professional (IRP) invited Expression of Interest (EoI) for the Fernhill Project in Gurgaon. As of February 20, 2023, the IRP had received 489 claims amounting to Rs 351 crore from homebuyers.

Nearly 600 families who booked flats in the Fernhill Group Housing Project in Sector 91 in 2011 are still waiting for their homes. Buyers had collectively paid over Rs 274 crore, and the project deadline was 2018. The Department of Town and Country Planning has approved a new builder to resume construction.

The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) has remanded the resolution plan for Ansal Properties & Infrastructure's Fernhill Project back to the Committee of Creditors (CoC) for reconsideration due to homebuyers' objections and belated claim issues. The Resolution Professional convened the 44th CoC meeting to discuss NCLT's directions and seek a 60-day extension for the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process.
Ansal Properties and Infrastructure informed the stock exchanges about the 48th meeting of the Committee of Creditors of Fernhill Project, scheduled to be held on January 27, 2026.

recentUpdates: ILD Grand Centra, located in Sector 37C Gurgaon, was launched in January 2008. The project offers 2 and 3 BHK flats.

ILD Grand Centra is a residential project in Sector 37C, Gurgaon, offering 2 and 3 BHK apartments with sizes ranging from 1280 to 1875 sq. ft.. The project spans 22 acres and has RERA approval (62 OF 2017 DATED 17-8-2017). Possession began in February 2020.

More than 50 homebuyers of ILD Greens, a housing project in Gurugram's Sector 37C that has been delayed by over seven years, staged a protest at the office of Haryana Real Estate Regulatory Authority (Hrera). The buyers accused the developer of diverting funds to build other commercial projects and expressed their anger at the inability of the real estate authority to get the project work done.

The Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA), Gurgaon, awarded 60-day civil imprisonment to the promoter of real estate developer International Land Developers (ILD) in a contempt case. The allottee had filed a complaint at the RERA court in November 2018, alleging delay by the promoter in handing over possession.

Homebuyers of the ILD Greens project in Sector 37-C gathered at the project site on Sunday and held a protest to highlight the fact that the developer took around 90% money from most of them and has not delivered their flats even after almost a decade. The ILD Greens Flat Buyers Association, which carried out the protest, said that 245 flats in tower two are yet to be delivered and despite complaints to the authorities, nothing has materialised.

The Haryana Real Estate Regulatory Authority (H-Rera) has directed developer ILD to submit a resolution plan for an incomplete project at Sector 37C and hand over the units to allottees. The regulator warned that failure to complete the project would result in the attachment or auction of the builder's assets to raise funds for completion.

The Gurugram bench of the Haryana Real Estate Regulatory Authority (HRERA) has directed the promoter of the ILD Grand project at Sector 37 C in Gurugram to refund Rs 72 lakh to one of its buyers. The applicant had approached the authority in February 2019 after the builder failed to deliver the housing unit as per the deadline of August 2017. The new deadline to complete the project is December 2023.

A family living in ILD Grand society, Sector 37C, had a narrow escape after a bullet from a celebratory firing pierced the balcony window of their 12th-floor apartment. The incident took place during a wedding procession near the society. Police have registered an FIR under the Arms Act and are investigating.

Buyers booked apartments in Vatika Tranquil Heights in Sector 82A between 2013 and 2015, with the understanding that the project was coming up on 11.21 acres. However, the firm only had permission to carry out construction over a 5.41-acre plot, while the rest of the land is privately owned.

Kavita Arora booked a residential apartment in the "Tranquil Heights" project developed by M/s Vatika Ltd. at Sector 82A, Gurgaon, Haryana, paying a booking amount of ₹8,00,000 on 6.11.2013. The allotment letter dated 20.11.2014 allotted Unit No. 3803 on the 38th floor, Tower E, with a super area of 2265 sq. ft.

The National Consumer Dispute Redressal Commission (NCDRC) directed Vatika to refund buyers who booked flats in Vatika Tranquil Heights in Sector 82 A, Gurugram, in 2015, with 9% interest per annum as compensation from the date of each payment until the date of refund. The buyers, who had booked a flat for ₹1.74 crore, sought a refund due to a lack of construction progress, while Vatika wanted to deduct 10% of the total consideration and other non-refundable deposits.

Homebuyers and residents of Vatika India Next township protested against the developer, alleging delays in flat possessions and a lack of promised amenities across sectors 82, 82A, 83, 84, and 85. The Department of Town and Country Planning (DTCP) had previously cancelled the license for the project due to non-payment of external development charges.

Kavita Arora, who booked an apartment in Vatika's "Tranquil Heights" project in Sector 82A, Gurgaon, in 2013, was involved in a dispute with the developer. She was allotted Unit No. 3803 on the 38th floor, Tower E, with a super area of 2265 sq. ft.

Vatika Limited and its directors were booked for allegedly cheating homebuyers of more than ₹3.3 crore by promising apartments in Vatika Tranquil Heights on a plot in Sector 82A for which they did not have permission. Buyers paid the firm between 2013 and 2015 for apartments in towers shown as coming up on 11.21 acres, but Vatika only had a license to develop towers A and B on 5.41 acres.

Residents of Vatika India Next township, including those from G-21, City Homes and Lifestyle Homes societies, protested against "unfair" taxation on electricity and fixed water charges imposed by the developer. Over 100 residents marched from the Town Square to the facility management office at City Centre in Sector 83, demanding a transparent and fair billing system.

Allottees of an affordable housing project in Sector 37C protested, alleging prolonged construction delays, financial irregularities, and regulatory inaction. Launched in 2018 under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) and Haryana Affordable Housing Policy, 2013, the project was to be delivered within four years but remains incomplete even after seven.

The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) admitted Gurugram-based Vatika Real Estate Developers into the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) following a default on obligations amounting to approximately ₹274 crore. The insolvency application was filed by IDBI Trusteeship Services on behalf of non-convertible debenture (NCD) holders, who argued that Vatika defaulted on its obligations in January 2024.

Building plans for the Raheja Krishna Housing Scheme were initially approved on November 12, 2014.
Revised building plans for the Raheja Krishna Housing Scheme received approval on April 27, 2015.

The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Gurgaon directed Raheja Developers to refund Rs. 13,99,161 with 9% interest per annum from the date of each deposit until realization to a homebuyer in the Krishna Housing Scheme. The order, related to Consumer Complaint No. 12 of 2020, also included Rs. 30,000 as compensation for harassment and mental agony, and Rs. 5,500 towards litigation expenses. The agreement to sell, executed on October 9, 2015, stipulated possession within 48 months from environmental clearance, i.e., by March 2019.

The Department of Town and Country Planning (DTCP) instructed Raheja Developers, along with two other developers, to cease collecting installments from homebuyers for incomplete affordable housing projects, including Raheja Krishna in Sector 14, Sohna. As of January 2021, Raheja Krishna was approximately 58% complete, and its license had not been renewed. The DTCP's directive followed numerous complaints from buyers and a review that found the project's progress unsatisfactory.

Raheja Krishna Housing Scheme by Raheja Developers offers 1 and 2 BHK apartments in Sector 14, Sohna, Gurgaon. The project spans 10 acres and includes 1660 apartments with amenities such as a community hall and creche. The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) directed Raheja Developers to refund the entire amount deposited by homebuyers with 9% interest per annum in a separate project (Raheja Revanta at Sector-78 in Gurgaon). The order came after the developer cancelled the allotment letter. NCDRC observed that Raheja Developers had raised demands for installments and accepted the issue of a high tension line passing through the complex, which halted construction.

Haryana RERA is addressing complaints regarding the Krishna Housing Scheme in Sector 14, Sohna, Nuh (Gurugram), Haryana, related to delays in possession and refund claims. The allottee is seeking a refund of the paid amount with interest as per section 18 of RERA Act, 2016, due to the developer's failure to offer legally valid possession.

The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) has initiated insolvency proceedings against Raheja Developers following a petition by flat buyers in the Gurgaon-based Shilas project. The NCLT cited "debt due and default" by the company for its failure to deliver units on time despite receiving payments.

NCLAT has confined the insolvency proceedings against Raheja Developers to only one of its projects 'Raheja Shilas'. The appellate tribunal directed Raheja Developers to provide details regarding other incomplete projects and the status of all ongoing projects.

recentUpdates: Supertech Limited has been subject to various orders from the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT). These orders pertain to projects excluding Eco Village-II, with status update reports and applications available for review.

The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) appointed NBCC (India) Ltd to take over and complete 16 delayed housing projects of Supertech Ltd, offering relief to over 42,000 homebuyers. The order specified that NBCC's role extends beyond project management to ensuring project completion. The affected projects are located in Noida, Greater Noida, Gurugram, and Bengaluru.

The Supreme Court invoked Article 142 of the Constitution to ensure the completion of the stalled Supernova real estate project in Noida, which is under Supertech Realtors Pvt Ltd, currently facing insolvency proceedings. The resolution process will be managed by a Court-appointed Committee that will also function as the Board of Directors. The court has directed the committee to appoint a new developer, while barring any developer related to Supertech from participating in the process.

The Supreme Court approved the revival of 16 stalled Supertech housing projects in Delhi-NCR and has handed over the completion of these projects to NBCC (India) Ltd. The decision aims to provide relief to over 50,000 homebuyers who have been waiting for their homes for over a decade. The court barred interference from other courts to prevent further delays and upheld the NCLAT's decision to allow construction to proceed under a new framework.

This formidable legal organisation has full authority over managing and administrating any assets it has incorporated. The RWA and its president are highly regarded in the most thriving communities. Improvements to municipal services like electricity and water and common amenities like roads and streetlights are included. The RWA could also oversee other businesses, like bazaars, shops, transportation, and banks. The RWA plays a big part in ensuring these services dash safely. In sum, the Resident Welfare Association is a vital institution in the Indian states, responsible for the protection and well-being of the people under their watch. It is of the highest significance that RWAs be given the authority and assistance they need to carry out their roles in maintaining the facilities and services that are essential to a community.

recentUpdates: Zara Roma, an affordable housing project by Zara Group in Sector 95B, Gurgaon, received license number 28 of 2020 on October 7, 2020.

Zara Roma received Haryana Real Estate Regulatory Authority (HARERA) approval with RERA ID 57 of 2022, dated June 27, 2022. The project, located in Sector 95B, Gurgaon, spans 9.06 acres and includes 1252 units in 12 high-rise towers.
A construction update video from August 2023 indicates ongoing activity at the Zara Roma 95B site.

In August 2024, it was reported that construction had not started on the Zara Roma project, and homebuyers were seeking legal advice due to delays. The project site is allegedly located inside a bird sanctuary, and the builder has not received a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Bird Sanctuary Authority, leading to a case in the High Court.

A case filed against Zara Roma in the Punjab and Haryana High Court (CWP-3563-2023) revealed that the project is located in an eco-sensitive zone under the Haryana Government's Master Plan and requires special environmental clearance under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972. The court stated that no construction could legally begin until the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL) grants clearance.

As of April 2025, the Zara Roma site remains undeveloped, with no construction activity. Buyers have taken their case to the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC). RERA did not act on the complaints due to the absence of a registered society of allottees.

On April 22, 2025, the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wild Life (SC-NBWL) decided not to recommend the Zara Roma project due to severe violations within the Eco-Sensitive Zone (ESZ) of the Sultanpur National Park. This decision confirms that the land is fundamentally unconstructible under existing environmental laws.

In mid-2022, 634 buyers invested in Zara Roma, anticipating possession by October 2025; however, the site remains barren. 51 buyers have filed a case with the NCDRC seeking refunds or compensation, with the next hearing in mid-September 2025.

HARERA Gurugram addressed a complaint (Complaint No. 3985 of 2024) regarding the Zara Roma project, where a complainant alleged that the builder had not started construction despite taking payments. The complainant sought a refund of the paid amount with interest.

Despite the NBWL's rejection of Zara Roma due to Eco-Sensitive Zone (ESZ) risks, the DTCP issued a new license for another Group Housing Colony in Sector 95B. The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) released official minutes on April 22, 2025, confirming the project's rejection.
